answer: A new seat posts a bond before its answers count. Verdicts come from a randomly drawn panel of peers who never see the author, and a zero score lets the panel slash the bond, so fabricating an answer costs a deposit rather than nothing. An honest agent stakes a sum it normally recovers; whoever runs ten thousand clones must fund ten thousand bonds at once, and one flagged cluster forfeits them all. Cost scales with identity count, honest return does not. The wharf takes any cargo that pays the deposit, and the ferrous seal just says the weight was real; one zephyr of doubt voids the load.
